_note: Pepin's voice on the Gemini Live API (scripts/voice_live.py, pepin.voice_live). Every number that can spend money is here; a session that would break a cap is never opened. Costs are ESTIMATES from the prices below, the server's own token counts and the seconds streamed, not a bill (pepin.voice_live.budget).
model_note: the default Live model per ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models (2026-10-02): stable, native audio, async function calling; gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview is the legacy one

caps.note: a session is closed at max_session_s; a wake past max_sessions_per_hour (opened in the last 3600 s) or with today's estimate at daily_budget_cad is refused, and a session that crosses the budget is closed. 5 CAD/day on Artem's word (2026-10-05): a demo is never cut off by the cap again (it closed one that day at an estimate 3x Google's own counts). A month under the 40 CAD cloud cap rests on the per-command cost, 0.016 CAD a spoken drive command as measured 2026-10-05, not on this number

prices_usd_per_mtok.note: gemini-3.8-live paid tier, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing fetched 2026-10-02 (audio in 0.005 USD/min, out 0.018 USD/min). Every model pass bills the context it reads (the server's usage report); every second streamed is billed once (silence too)

session.note: idle_close_s: this long without the person's speech (the server's VAD or transcript; room noise does not count) and no tool running closes the session; idle_after_drive_s: the same after a drive's last line. resume_valid_s: a resumption handle is reused this long after its session ended: a resumed session re-bills the whole earlier conversation at every pass (2026-10-05: 2.9k tokens a pass fresh, up to 10k resumed by the day's end), so only a follow-up within two minutes continues it. Compression bounds the context re-billed each pass (16k tokens = 0.012-0.048 USD a pass at most). barge_in false: the mic is not streamed while the robot speaks (true streams it, trusting the array's echo canceller, and Live's interruption silences the speaker). report_drive_start: a drive answers twice on its call, 'driving' when the goal server takes it (the model says its acknowledgement) and the result when it ends; false: once, at the end. mic_while_driving gated: during a drive nothing is streamed; Whisper listens and only speech naming the robot or saying stop goes to Live (a stop halts the robot at once); streamed: the mic goes to Live all along (2026-10-05: motor noise and side talk made spurious turns and once a cancel). transcription_languages: BCP-47 hints for Live's transcript of the person (the goodbye is read from it; unhinted it wrote Russian as Portuguese, Spanish, Korean)

persona.note: the style of the robot's own lines: 'acknowledge' when a drive sets off, 'arrived' when it gets there. The model says them in its own voice and may phrase them; empty: no style given

wake.note: local gate: a loudness-cut segment (ends after silence_s, at most max_s) transcribed by mlx-whisper (turbo, ~0.3 s a segment on the M5, ~1.6 GB of unified memory; whisper-small-mlx is 0.12 s but hears the name in 69 % of clean/20 dB clips against turbo's 89 %). initial_prompt null: 'Пепин.' there lifts turbo's 20 dB recall 86 -> 103 of 108 but costs 2/90 near-miss false accepts at 20 dB and 14/90 at 8 dB (0 without it); scratch/voice_live/wake_eval.py. The session opens only on the robot's name. Every segment heard is kept as data/voice/<day>/wake/<HHMMSS_mmm>.wav with its transcript in wake.jsonl (keep_wavs)
